author: Mark Atwood
text:
Investigated for landing in /do-beads JMAP-jfia. Two obstructions made me file `human` instead of landing:

**Obstruction 1: coherence conflict blocks the symmetric `impl<E> From<E> for BackendSetError<E>`.**

`BackendSetError` already has `impl<E> From<SetError> for BackendSetError<E>` (backend.rs:564). Adding `impl<E> From<E> for BackendSetError<E>` would conflict for `E = SetError`. Removing the existing `From<SetError>` impl is a breaking change (every consumer using `SetError::into()` to construct `BackendSetError::SetError(...)` breaks). So the ergonomic `?`-wrap half of the BackendChangesError symmetry cannot be added without a major bump.

**Obstruction 2: the redaction half has a wire-shape footgun the changes path does not have.**

A blanket `impl<E: std::error::Error> From<BackendSetError<E>> for JmapError` that maps BOTH arms to `server_fail(SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC)` would silently convert per-object `SetError` envelopes into method-level `serverFail` errors whenever a handler writes `?` on a `Result<X, BackendSetError<E>>`. Per RFC 8620 §5.3 a per-object SetError belongs in the `notCreated`/`notUpdated`/`notDestroyed` map, NOT as a method-level error. The handler MUST destructure first. So the ergonomic `?` path actively destroys correctness on the SetError arm — that's worse than the current hand-roll opportunity-to-leak.

**Confirmed wire-leak in the wild (separate concern, separate fix):**

`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mdn.rs:462-466` directly interpolates `BackendSetError::Other(e).to_string()` into a wire `description` field on the per-object SetError envelope. That IS the leak class .1 closed for changes. Should be filed against jmap-mail-server, not blocked on this decision. (The mdn.rs author hand-rolled the conversion and got the per-object SetError shape right but the description-string wrong.)

**Options I considered, ranked:**

(a) **Named method, no From impls.** Add `BackendSetError::into_set_error_or_method_error(self) -> Result<SetError, JmapError>` (or similar shape). The method-error arm uses SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC. Handler writes `match be.into_set_error_or_method_error() { Ok(se) => not_x.insert(id, se.into_wire()), Err(je) => return Err(je) }`. No `?` path, no conflict with `From<SetError>`, no SetError→method-error footgun. Asymmetric with changes but the per-object/per-method shape mismatch makes that asymmetry honest. Closes the leak class with structural enforcement.

(b) **From<BackendSetError<E>> for JmapError that panics on the SetError arm (debug) / server_fails (release).** Catches the misuse loudly in dev but still gives `?`. Aggressive; I'd want explicit sign-off.

(c) **Status quo + lint guidance in `BackendSetError` rustdoc.** Document the hand-roll pattern in the rustdoc with a copy-paste-able example, audit every existing `*-server` consumer for the leak, file separate consumer beads for any leak found. Doesn't add API surface. Doesn't structurally prevent the next consumer's leak.

(d) **Full symmetry at major-bump.** Drop `From<SetError>` (replaced by explicit `BackendSetError::set_error(se)` constructor), add blanket `From<E>`, add From<BackendSetError<E>> with documented semantics. Lands at the next major.

**Recommendation: (a).** Closes the leak class with a structural surface (the named method is the One Right Way). No conflict with existing From<SetError>. No SetError→method-error wire regression. Asymmetric with BackendChangesError but the asymmetry is intentional and matches the underlying spec semantics (changes errors are always method-level; set errors are typed per-object). The accompanying audit for `mdn.rs`-class leaks gets its own bead per `*-server` sibling.

The finding's body suggests something like `into_jmap_error_or_set_error(self) -> Result<JmapError, SetError>`; I prefer the SetError-as-Ok shape because SetError is the expected case (per RFC 8620 §5.3 the SetError variant is the typed per-object case; the method-error is the bail-out). Both shapes are reasonable.

Whichever option is chosen, the workspace propagation pass needs to:
1. Land the named method (or chosen surface) in jmap-server.
2. Audit every `crate-jmap-*-server/` consumer for hand-rolled BackendSetError matches; convert to the new surface.
3. File a separate bead for the mdn.rs wire-leak fix.

Releasing claim. Bead remains open with `human` label.
